units.menuHint.motion: Speed, fuel economy, acceleration, force, torque and pressure.
units.menuHint.energy: Energy, power, charge, voltage, current and resistance.
units.menuHint.scientific: Density, frequency, angle, concentration, prefixes, light and flow.

units.smart.title: Quick convert
units.smart.nothingTyped: Type a value to see it converted.
units.smart.notANumber: This is not a number. Write it with digits, for example 12.5 or 1,250.
units.smart.ambiguous: This number can be read two ways. It was read with “{mark}” before the decimals, as the language of the program writes numbers.
units.smart.measured: Measured, not defined: its last digits may change when it is measured again.
units.smart.failed: The value could not be converted.
units.smart.pin: Pin: keep this unit first in the lists
units.smart.popularNote: {count, plural, other {Only the popular units are listed here. The table has all # units of this converter.}}
units.hint.unitsPanel: Shows or folds the panel of units beside the table.
units.hint.rowNumbers: Shows or hides the number of each row of the table.
units.hint.extremesInFull: On: values too large or too small are written with every zero. Off: with a power of ten, as 1.6 × 10⁻³⁵.
units.leave.title: Leave this table?
units.leave.lead: The table has values. Going to another converter in this tab loses them.
units.panel.title: Units

units.panel.takeOut: Take its column out of the table
units.panel.pin: Pin as a favourite: it comes first here and in Quick convert

units.active.removeNamed: Take the column “{unit}” out of the table
units.bar.fit: Fit the columns to the table
units.bar.fitHint: Puts the columns back in order: every width you dragged or fitted goes, and the columns share the width of the table equally again
units.hint.smart: Goes to the first page of Units, Quick convert: one value converted quickly from a unit to another.

units.table.nothingPasted: There was nothing to put in the table.
units.table.clipboardRefused: The clipboard could not be reached.
units.table.tooLarge: That is too much at once. Export to a file instead, or select fewer rows.
units.table.notRead: The file could not be read.
units.table.notWritten: The file could not be written.
units.table.notANumber: Row {row}: this is not a number, so nothing is converted

units.own.newHint: Make a unit of your own in this converter
units.own.lead: A unit of your own in “{converter}”. Say it by a unit that exists, and it converts to every other one.
units.own.name: Name
units.own.factor: How many of the unit it is said by make one
units.own.offset: Added after multiplying, in {reference} (for a scale that starts elsewhere)
units.own.toReference: From {symbol} to {reference}, with x for the value
units.own.fromReference: Back from {reference} to {symbol}, with x for the value
units.own.formulaHint: Arithmetic (+ − × ÷ ^ and brackets), x, pi, e, and sqrt, abs, ln, log, log2, exp, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan. Decimals with a point. A formula is worked out, never run as a program.
units.own.noValue: One of it has no value in the base unit.
units.own.notUndone: the way back does not undo the formula
units.own.removed: {count, plural, one {# unit of yours removed} other {# units of yours removed}}
units.own.error.id: A unit with this id is already there.
units.own.error.name: The unit needs a name of at most 80 letters.
units.own.error.reference: The unit it is said by is not one this unit can be said by.
units.own.error.factor: The factor must be a number that is not zero, for example 0.75 or 5/9.
units.own.error.offset: What is added must be a number.
units.own.error.one-way: Write a factor, or a formula with its way back.
units.own.error.no-way-back: Write the way back too: the formula from the other unit to this one.
units.own.error.no-x: Each formula must use x, the value that is converted.
units.own.error.too-deep: The formula has too many brackets inside one another.
units.own.error.number: Letter {at}: this is not a number.
units.own.error.name-unknown: Letter {at}: this word is not known. Use x, pi, e or one of the functions listed.
units.own.error.bracket: Letter {at}: a bracket is missing here.
units.own.error.expected: Letter {at}: a number, x or a bracket is expected here.
units.own.error.left-over: Letter {at}: something is left over here. An operator may be missing.
units.own.error.too-many: A converter takes at most 500 units of your own.
units.own.error.other: Another unit of yours can no longer be read. Change or remove it first.
units.column.everywhereHint: The precision of this column becomes the precision of its unit: in every table and in Quick convert. Settings lists it.
units.bar.startWith: Start this converter with these columns
units.table.startsWith: Tables of this converter now start with these columns
units.table.precisionEverywhere: This precision is now the unit's, everywhere
units.settings.ownTab: Open each converter in a tab of its own
units.settings.ownTabHint: Off: a converter chosen from the menus takes the place of the one in the tab, and asks first when its table has values.
units.settings.thousandsHint: What is written between the thousands of large numbers. Typing and pasting understand every way.
units.settings.precisionNote: Each unit has its own decimals. Choose a converter, find a unit and set the decimals it is written with everywhere. “Use for this unit everywhere” in the menu of a column sets the same value.
units.settings.precisionNoneChanged: You have changed no unit yet. Choose a converter above to see its units.
units.settings.precisionOwn: {decimals, plural, one {Its own: # decimal} other {Its own: # decimals}}
units.settings.precisionBack: Back to the unit's own precision
units.settings.startingNote: A table starts with the units its converter ships with. To change them, set the columns of a table as you want them and choose “Start this converter with these columns” in the table options. The converters you changed are listed here.
units.settings.startingBack: Back to the units the converter ships with
units.settings.ownNote: Units you made, of every converter. A new one is made in the units panel of its converter, with “New unit”; it is changed there too.
units.settings.own.exportNote: Your units as text. Copy it and keep it in a file, or paste it in Settings on another computer.
units.settings.own.importNote: Paste here the text that “Export” gave. Its units are added to yours; one with the same id takes the place of yours.
units.settings.own.read: {count, plural, one {# unit added} other {# units added}}
units.settings.own.notRead: This text holds no units. Paste what “Export” gave, whole.
units.settings.reset: Put the settings of Units back as they shipped
units.rates.old: old: they could not be read again
units.rates.offline: Reading rates from the network is off in Settings.
units.rates.refreshHint: Reads the rates again. Currencies change once a day at their source, so they are read again at most once an hour; cryptocurrencies at most once a minute.
units.rates.sourcesHint: The two services the rates come from. Help → Units → Currency says more, with their addresses.
units.settings.ratesCredit: Name the sources beside the rates
units.settings.ratesCreditHint: On: the names of the two services (ExchangeRate-API, CoinGecko) are shown, small, on the line that says when the rates are of. The manual has their own words and their addresses.
units.settings.currencyNote: Currencies have no fixed factor: their rates are read from two free services while the currency converter is used. Only the rates are asked for: nothing about you, and never the amounts you convert. The manual names the services.
units.settings.ratesOnline: Read the rates from the network
units.settings.ratesOnlineHint: Off: the currency converter uses the last rates it kept, however old, and asks nothing.
